title: Five-day windows showed no clear added SWPC storm outlook skill over recurrence in 2018-2025
abstract: We tested whether timing tolerance reveals added skill in NOAA SWPC 27-day numerical outlooks. We reused a fixed published archive and fit probability models on 2010-2017. In 2018-2025, the five-day event test used 6,384 forecasts from 400 issues on 2,903 target dates. Adding issued outlook values to a recurrence model with the same event window reduced Brier error by 1.43%, with conditional 95% 112-day block limits of -1.58% to +4.57%. One-, three- and seven-day tests also gave no clear gain. A new diagnostic conditioned each issue on its observed storm-day count. It removed a common issue-wide odds level and tested placement of storm days. The placement log-score gain was 1.53% (-1.15% to +4.09%) in 273 informative issues. An exact count-plus-placement score split gave uncertain gains in both parts. These controls did not expose a clear hidden timing gain. The method uses established conditional probability results. This is a retrospective application to the same archive, not independent validation or a measurement of solar wind arrival error. Eight test years, one probability model, revised historic inputs and an independent-day candidate joint law limit inference. Code, source entry hashes, original data provenance, fitted models, aggregate scores and checks are included. External record tables stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Added Brier skill over a recurrence model with the same event window. Conditional 95% intervals use 112-calendar-day blocks. All four intervals include zero.

citations.reason: Reuses its verified full weekly forecast and observation tables. Adds timing-window models and a count-versus-placement score diagnostic on the same archive.
Short-lead physical attribution motivates care in separating arrival error from activity level; we do not test its solar wind observations.
